prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas. Injury: wrist fracture. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1091; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, so you can just refer to me as the plaintiff.

Q: That's fine for today. Where were you on the day of the collision?

A: I was driving home from work on a county road in Houston, Texas, heading east toward my neighborhood.

Q: What time of day was it?

A: It was in the late afternoon, around rush hour, so traffic was heavy and moving slowly.

Q: Describe the vehicle you were driving.

A: It was my own sedan, a compact model I've had for several years. It was in good condition before the accident.

Q: Tell me what happened as you approached the point of impact.

A: A pickup truck came over into my lane. I braked and turned the wheel, but we still collided head-on. It wasn't a high-speed crash. Both cars were moving slowly, but the impact was enough to jolt me forward and then back.

Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head?

A: No, I didn't black out. I remember everything clearly. My head didn't hit anything, but my right hand hit the steering wheel and then the dashboard.

Q: When did you first realize you were hurt?

A: Within a few minutes my wrist started to swell and throb. I could barely grip anything, so I knew it was more than a bruise.

Q: Who took you for medical care?

A: The paramedics checked me at the scene, and then I was taken to an emergency room. They took X-rays and told me the wrist was fractured.

Q: What treatment have you received since then?

A: They put me in a splint first. Later I saw an orthopedic specialist who set the bone more precisely and put me in a cast. I've also had several follow-up appointments and some physical therapy to regain movement.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?

A: It's made a lot of things harder. I'm right-handed, so simple tasks like buttoning a shirt, cooking, or typing take much longer. I had to ask family members for help with laundry and grocery shopping for a while. I also had to take time away from my job, which has been stressful.

Q: Have you had any difficulty sleeping or with hobbies?

A: Yes. I used to play recreational softball on weekends, and I haven't been able to play since the accident. I also wake up at night when I roll onto my wrist, and the ache can linger through the day.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else about the accident or your injuries you'd like to add?

A: Only that I'm still in physical therapy, and my doctor has said I may have some stiffness for a while. I'm hopeful I'll get back to normal, but I'm not there yet.
